content.comment_body: Good morning everyone. Can anyone explain this issue? I have marker points M25 (white backlight), M28 (amber), and M29 (red). When working in my current network project, created and edited with [product_name] [version_no], I am able to select and move the descriptions for M25 and M29, but not for M28. If I create a new diagram and place these markers in the same version of [product_name], the font appears odd and none of the marker descriptions can be moved. Is there a workaround to position description text as desired? See attached video for clarification.

Hello. I've noticed similar unusual behaviors in [product_name] software, especially with newer versions. With [version_no], I can confirm some newly introduced issues. You can use the 'Insert comment' tool as a workaround: activate the tool, select the text entry, and simply close the popup window—no editing required. Afterwards, the marker symbol can be moved and the font adjusted.

I'm not sure what steps you've taken. Without editing, you can't move the comment text for markers or alter the font, though the text can be highlighted. As shown in the video, use the 'Insert Comment' function, and you can then select, move, and change the font of the comment.

Thank you! That's exactly what was needed. I simply had to interact with the description text using the Text edit tool, which then unlocked the text and allowed it to remain editable. It's a quirky behavior! Thanks for the fast assistance. This tip should be more widely known. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users describe unpredictable behavior when trying to position and edit description text for marker points in [product_name] [version_no]. Some markers can be manipulated as intended, while others are locked, even within the same session. Starting new diagrams often results in poor font appearance and locked descriptions, confusing users and affecting productivity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a reliable and straightforward process for placing and editing marker description text, regardless of diagram origin or creation time, with consistent functionality across markers in [product_name].
